test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A train P, going at the speed of 30 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 296 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 21 km/hr, in 6.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to cross completely train R of length 196 m, going at 96 km/hr in the opposite direction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 30 − 21 = 9 kmph = 9 × 5/18 = 2.5 m/s.

Total distance (LP + LQ) = Speed × Time = 2.5 × (6.5 × 60) = 2.5 × 390 = 975 m.

Length of Train P (LP) = 975 − 296 = 679 m.

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 30 + 96 = 126 kmph = 126 × 5/18 = 35 m/s.

Time to cross R = (LP + LR) ÷ Relative speed = (679 + 196) ÷ 35 = 875 ÷ 35 = 25 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a383d9b18b24a1d08f1bf342934fb037935c695eab33d27abc31f577eacb1dd5.png] 

**Given:** Speed P = 30 kmph, Speed Q = 21 kmph, Length Q = 296 m, Time 1 = 6.5 min, Speed R = 96 kmph, Length R = 196 m.

**Formula Used:** Time = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ Relative Speed; kmph to m/s = × 5/18.

⇒ Relative Speed P & Q = (30 − 21) × 5/18 = 9 × 5/18 = 2.5 m/s.

⇒ Total Length (LP + LQ) = Speed × Time = 2.5 × (6.5 × 60) = 975 m.

⇒ Length of P (LP) = 975 − 296 = 679 m.

⇒ Relative Speed P & R = (30 + 96) × 5/18 = 126 × 5/18 = 35 m/s.

⇒ Total Distance for P & R = 679 + 196 = 875 m.

⇒ Required Time = 875 ÷ 35 = 25 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is (S₁ − S₂). When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is (S₁ + S₂).

Crossing Length Rule

When a train crosses another train, bridge, or platform, the total distance covered is always the **sum of their lengths** (L₁ + L₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p
